title: 0402-expected-hypothetical-completion-probability
universal_lens: Expected Hypothetical Completion Probability (EHCP) unifies quarterback decision-making and receiver catchability through conditional logistic modeling of play trajectories. Expected Hypothetical Completion Probability (EHCP) integrates Bayesian logistic modeling with BART-based imputation of unobservables, enabling probabilistic inference over pass outcomes.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian logistic regression with N(0,1) priors to infer completion likelihood from tracked player states, enabling probabilistic verdicts on QB decisions. GSI employs Bayesian logistic regression with empirical imputation to compute EHCP, propagating uncertainty through posterior draws for real-time decision support.
gse_mapping: GSE models situational state transitions using EHCP as a dynamic reward signal, updating receiver catchability estimates post-snap via gradient-boosted trees. GSE uses EHCP as a situational state variable, tracking receiver-level probabilities to inform dynamic play-calling and receiver prioritization during live gameplay.

primitives.name: Expected Hypothetical Completion Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Completion-probability model**: logistic form log(P(y_i=1|x_i)/P(y_i=0|x_i)) = f(x_i), i.e., P = [1+e^{-f(x)}]^{-1}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_i': 'binary indicator for completion (1 = caught, 0 = incomplete/intercepted)', 'x_i': 'vector of covariates including receiver position, velocity, QB release timing, and spatial context', 'f(x_i)': 'linear or nonlinear function of x_i mapping to log-odds scale'}
primitives.assumptions: Conditional independence of outcomes given features; logistic link function captures nonlinearity in probability space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When x_i contains extreme outliers or missing tracking data, model outputs become unreliable.

layer2.mapping: EHCP serves as a probabilistic kernel for evaluating route efficiency and QB targeting accuracy in GSE’s decision graph.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive probability of catch given trajectory and timing.

primitives.name: Bayesian Logistic Regression Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Two estimators compared: (a) Bayesian logistic regression with independent N(0,1) priors on θ after Gelman et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ': 'regression coefficients vector', 'X': 'design matrix of player state variables', 'y': 'binary outcome vector for completion', 'σ': 'logistic sigmoid function'}
primitives.assumptions: Prior distributions are conjugate; model assumes linear relationship in latent logit space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model fails when feature correlation exceeds threshold or sample size is insufficient for convergence.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI’s probabilistic inference engine where θ represents learned parameters of player behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior mean estimates of coefficient vectors for each play type.

primitives.name: NFL Tracking Data Schema
primitives.verbatim_quote: Per player/ball per frame: timestamp, x (0–120 yd), y (0–53.3 yd), speed (yd/s), distance since prior frame, direction (0–360°), tagged events (snap, pass release, catch, tackle), player ID/name/jersey/team, frame ID, game ID, play ID.
primitives.latex: \mathcal{T} = \{(t, x, y, v, d, \theta, E, p, n, j, T, G, P)\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'timestamp in seconds', 'x, y': 'position coordinates in yards', 'v': 'speed in yards per second', 'd': 'distance traveled since last frame', 'θ': 'direction in degrees', 'E': 'event tag (snap, pass release, etc.)', 'p': 'player identifier', 'n': 'player name', 'j': 'jersey number', 'T': 'team identifier', 'G': 'game ID', 'P': 'play ID'}
primitives.assumptions: Data is synchronized across frames and annotated with event tags.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of synchronization or mislabeled events leads to invalid trajectory reconstruction.

layer2.mapping: Provides input structure for both GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s state transition logic.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal alignment and event tagging integrity check metrics.

primitives.name: Expected Hypothetical Completion Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: **EHCP**: EHCP(x*_obs) = E_{x*_miss}[F(x*_obs, x*_miss)] ≈ (1/M) Σ_{m=1}^{M} F(x*_obs, x*^(m)_miss), computed per posterior draw of f to propagate model uncertainty; report posterior mean and 95% interval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x^*_\\text{obs}': 'Observable covariates at throw time (dimensionless)', 'x^*_\\text{miss}': 'Unobservable covariates at catch attempt (dimensionless)', 'F': 'Bayesian logistic model function (probability scale)', 'M': 'Number of imputed samples (integer)'}
primitives.assumptions: Model assumes independence of observables and unobservables, and that the posterior draws accurately represent model uncertainty.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When x^*_\text{miss} cannot be meaningfully imputed due to data sparsity or extreme variance.

layer2.mapping: EHCP serves as a derived kernel for GSI's probabilistic inference engine, enabling dynamic pass outcome prediction under hypotheticals.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior mean and 95% credible interval of EHCP per receiver

primitives.name: Empirical Imputation of Unobservables
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Imputation of unobservables**: for a hypothetical pass, covariates split into x*_obs (measurable up to throw time) and x*_miss (speed/direction at catch attempt; receiver/defender/ball pairwise distances at arrival; total distance run snap→catch; ball air time; changes in speed/separation/direction/distance while ball in air).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x^*_\\text{obs}': 'Observable features at throw time (dimensionless)', 'x^*_\\text{miss}': 'Unobservable features at catch attempt (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Unobservables are drawn from marginal empirical distributions of observed passes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When empirical distributions lack sufficient variation or coverage for valid sampling.

layer2.mapping: Imputation mirrors GSE’s state transition logic by filling missing state variables with empirical analogues.
layer2.telemetry: Sampled x^*_\text{miss} from empirical distribution of observed passes

primitives.name: Bayesian Logistic Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Bayesian logistic: π(θ|y) ∝ π(θ)·p(y|θ); prior π(θ_j) = N(0,1) independently after Gelman-2008 rescaling.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y': 'Binary outcome (completion or not)', 'x': 'Input feature vector (dimensionless)', 'f(x)': 'Logit function (log-odds scale)', 'θ': 'Regression coefficients (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Coefficients follow normal priors, and model is linear in log-odds space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When data is insufficient to constrain posterior or when non-linearity dominates.

layer2.mapping: Serves as core predictive operator in GSI's Bayesian inference pipeline for pass completion likelihood.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior mean of θ and 95% credible intervals

primitives.name: Conditional Imputation for EHCP
primitives.verbatim_quote: EHCP layer: replace marginal imputation with a **conditional imputation model** — predict x_miss | x_obs (route-type-conditioned distributional regression or a small normalizing flow per route family); then EHCP = Monte-Carlo average exactly as in equation (2).

primitives.breakdown_regime: When EHCP ≈ fitted probability across all receivers, indicating collapse of hypothetical layer.

reasoning_traces.think: The foundational premise of EHCP lies in modeling the conditional probability of a pass being completed given observed player positions, velocities, and timing. This approach shifts focus from outcome-based evaluation to process-based analysis—critical for understanding quarterback decision quality. The paper introduces two estimators: Bayesian logistic regression and BART, each offering distinct advantages in interpretability versus flexibility. The former provides principled uncertainty quantification while the latter excels at capturing complex interactions among variables without strong parametric assumptions. In GSI, these models can be adapted into a hierarchical Bayesian framework that updates completion likelihood dynamically during a play using real-time tracking data. For GSE, the EHCP becomes an integral part of the agent’s belief system, informing decisions about optimal target selection and route execution. The schema defines how to encode such data, ensuring consistency between empirical observations and theoretical constructs. A key insight is that EHCP must be computed conditionally rather than marginally to avoid bias introduced by unobserved confounders like defensive pressure or weather conditions. reasoning_traces.think: The chapter introduces Expected Hypothetical Completion Probability (EHCP) as a core probabilistic construct for evaluating pass outcomes under hypothetical scenarios. It leverages Bayesian logistic regression with BART-based model selection to ensure robustness. The process begins with observable features at throw time (x*_obs), which are augmented with imputed unobservables (x*_miss) drawn from empirical distributions of actual passes. These imputations allow for simulation of catch-time conditions, including speed, direction, and spatial relationships. The EHCP is then computed as an expectation over these imputed scenarios using the logistic model F. This approach enables GSI to quantify uncertainty in pass completion likelihood, informing real-time decisions. The use of posterior draws ensures propagation of model uncertainty, yielding both point estimates and credible intervals. The method is validated via 10-fold cross-validation using MSE, log-loss, and misclassification metrics, confirming BART's superiority. This framework supports GSE's dynamic situational awareness by providing receiver-level EHCP scores, enabling identification of optimal pass targets based on expected outcomes. This modification allows for more accurate estimation of catch probabilities under hypothetical scenarios, particularly when certain trajectory features are missing. The use of route-type-conditioned distributional regression or normalizing flows enables nuanced modeling of how different pass routes influence the likelihood of a catch. Additionally, the chapter emphasizes improving model fidelity through time-ordered validation and gradient boosting techniques, which offer both speed and scalability compared to traditional Bayesian approaches like BART. The inclusion of QB-pressure features further enriches the model’s understanding of situational context. Finally, an extension to Expected Hypothetical EPA (EHEPA) is proposed, shifting from binary catch targets to continuous point values, thereby addressing limitations in current EHCP formulations and offering deeper insights into play value.
